title: Derived strict-tower evaluation comparisons, normalization and computing class
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ be the category of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system], and use unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B},Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)},Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B)}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with independent morphism universe bounds. The index $n\in\mathbf N$ denotes positive level $n+1$. Write $e_n^{\mathcal A}$ for ordinary evaluation, $E_n^{\mathcal A}=D(e_n^{\mathcal A})$ for its exact derived descent, and $\lambda^{\mathcal A}_{n,P}:E_n^{\mathcal A}(Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)}P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal A}(P_n)$ for the canonical localization factor. For an additive functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, let $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be its levelwise extension and $C(F)$ its termwise action on cochain complexes. Define $\iota_{F,n}:C(F^{\operatorname{Tow}})C(e_n^{\mathcal B})\xrightarrow{\sim}C(e_n^{\mathcal A})C(F)$ by the degreewise identity (composition here is in Lean order). For arbitrary functors $L:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $L_t:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B))$, define $\operatorname{Comparison}(L,L_t,n)$ to be the type of natural isomorphisms $v:L_t E_n^{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n^{\mathcal A}L$, again in Lean composition order. Given natural transformations $\epsilon:Q_{\mathcal A}L\to C(F)Q_{\mathcal B}$, $\tau:Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)}L_t\to C(F^{\operatorname{Tow}})Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B)}$ and any predicate $\mathrm{good}$ on tower complexes, define $\operatorname{IsNormalizedOn}(F,L,L_t,\epsilon,\tau,\mathrm{good},n,v)$ to mean that for every tower complex $P$ satisfying $\mathrm{good}(P)$ the following equation holds (the symbol $\gg$ means first the left arrow, then the right arrow):
$$v_{Q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)}P}\gg L(\lambda^{\mathcal A}_{n,P})\gg\epsilon_{P_n}=E_n^{\mathcal B}(\tau_P)\gg\lambda^{\mathcal B}_{n,C(F^{\operatorname{Tow}})P}\gg Q_{\mathcal B}(\iota_{F,n,P}).$$
For $a\le b$, define $\operatorname{derivedTransition}(a,b)$ to be the natural transformation $E_b^{\mathcal A}\to E_a^{\mathcal A}$ obtained by localization of the termwise ordinary evaluation transformation induced by the unique arrow $\operatorname{op}b\to\operatorname{op}a$; this includes $a=b$.

In a chosen common universe $u$, for a small site $\mathcal C$ with object type in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$ and a sheaf of commutative rings $R$ with values in $\mathrm{CommRingCat}_u$, let $\operatorname{Modules}(R)$ be the existing category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the underlying sheaf of rings of $R$. For $P\in\mathrm{CoCh}(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Modules}(R)))$, define $\operatorname{IsGoodTower}(R,P)$ to mean that for every $k\in\mathbf N$ the evaluated complex $P_k$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and for every $k\in\mathbf N$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ its term $P_k^q$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. These are definitions only: no universality, resolution, existence or uniqueness theorem is asserted.

lean.statement:
def IsNormalizedOn (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (L : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (Lt : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B))
    (ε : (DerivedCategory.Q (C := A)) ⋙ L ⟶
      F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ (DerivedCategory.Q (C := B)))
    (τ : (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)) ⋙ Lt ⟶
      ((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ A B).obj F).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B)))
    (good : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ → Prop) (n : ℕ)
    (v : Comparison (A := A) (B := B) L Lt n) : Prop
